etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Late Latin aequivocus +‎ -al, from aequus +‎ vocō. By surface analysis, equi- +‎ vocal.
senses: Having two or more equally applicable meanings; capable of double or multiple interpretation.
Capable of being ascribed to different motives, or of signifying opposite feelings, purposes, or characters; deserving to be suspected.
(philosophy) A word or expression capable of different meanings; an ambiguous term.
